subject_line: The prose poems of adoption in In Praise of Late Wonder
email_body:
Dear Lee,

In Praise of Late Wonder gathers more than twenty-five memoir-like prose poems about your adoption from Daejeon. You once said adoption is usually framed as purely a blessing, while it is also wrapped in trauma, and the new book seems to live inside that tension.

For a Spotlight, I would love to ask why the prose poem became the right form for this material now.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. The portrait is developed through a few written questions, which you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part?

Best regards,
The Author Ledger

subject_line: The Raven's Gift and its second life in 2020
email_body:
Dear Don,

The Anchorage Daily News profile last year noted how The Raven's Gift found renewed interest in 2020, when its epidemic story suddenly felt prophetic. It also mentioned that, besides the novel and a poetry collection, you have co-written two memoirs for other people.

For a Spotlight, I would like to ask how shaping someone else's life story differs from inventing your own, and what the Yup'ik villages you return to teach in have given your writing.

subject_line: From An Irritable Métis to Becoming Little Shell
email_body:
Dear Chris,

Your weekly newsletter, An Irritable Métis, and your memoir Becoming Little Shell seem to come from the same place: a long, patient look at what belonging means, written from near Frenchtown. Serving as Montana's Poet Laureate after that book must have put you in front of many new rooms of readers.

For a Spotlight, I would like to ask how writing a weekly letter shaped the memoir, and what the laureate years taught you about speaking for a place.

subject_line: Living beneath the dam in West Central Idaho
email_body:
Dear CMarie,

Camped Beneath the Dam, your 2020 collection from Floodgate, has a title that carries a whole landscape and a pressure inside it. Knowing that you write from the mountains of West Central Idaho, and served as the state's writer in residence before becoming Poet Laureate, made me curious how place and public role meet in your work.

For a Spotlight, I would like to ask what the dam in that title holds back for you.

book_title: The Tao of Raven: An Alaska Native Memoir
subject_line: Raven's way through The Tao of Raven
email_body:
Dear Ernestine,

The Tao of Raven, your 2016 memoir from University of Washington Press, appeared shortly before you were named Alaska State Writer Laureate. I also read that you only reluctantly retired from teaching at the University of Alaska Southeast in 2018.

For a Spotlight, I would like to ask what Raven's presence allowed you to say in that book that plain memoir could not, and what your writing life in Juneau has looked like since leaving the classroom.
